questions.q: Fundamental human rights can best be defined as entitlements and privileges that...
options: are granted exclusively to citizens of high social or economic status.
are inalienable and inherently belong to every individual by virtue of being human.
are created by political parties to reward their active members.
can only be enjoyed during periods of national economic prosperity.
questions.explain: **Fundamental human rights** are universal, inalienable moral and legal entitlements inherent to every person simply because they are human, irrespective of nationality, sex, ethnicity, religion, or social standing.

questions.q: The right to work, fair wages, education, and access to healthcare belong to which category of human rights?
questions.explain:
Human rights are broadly classified into three generations:

| Generation | Category | Key Examples |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **First Generation** | Civil & Political | Right to life, liberty, fair hearing, voting |
| **Second Generation** | Economic, Social & Cultural | Right to work, education, healthcare, fair wages |
| **Third Generation** | Solidarity / Environmental | Right to clean environment, peace, self-determination |

questions.q: In the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Fundamental Human Rights are explicitly enshrined in...
questions.explain: **Chapter IV** (Sections 33–46) of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria contains the provisions on Fundamental Human Rights, including the right to life, dignity, personal liberty, fair hearing, and freedoms of thought, expression, and movement.

questions.q: The fundamental characteristic which states that human rights cannot be taken away or transferred from an individual is known as...
questions.explain: **Inalienability** means human rights cannot be surrendered, sold, transferred, or arbitrarily taken away by the state or any authority, except through due process of law.

questions.q: The **universality** of human rights implies that these rights...
options: apply equally to all human beings everywhere without discrimination.
are subject to modification based on personal wealth and status.
are enforceable only in economically developed nations.
can only be enjoyed within an individual's country of birth.
questions.explain: **Universality** means that all human rights apply equally and without discrimination to every person in every part of the world, regardless of race, gender, nationality, or faith.

questions.q: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was formally adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on...
questions.explain: The **UDHR** was proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly in Paris on **10th December, 1948** (Resolution 217 A). This date is commemorated globally every year as International Human Rights Day.

questions.q: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was proclaimed in Paris primarily as a direct global response to the atrocities committed during the...
questions.explain: Following the devastation and genocide of the **Second World War (1939–1945)**, the international community formed the United Nations and created the UDHR to ensure such barbarous acts would never recur.

questions.q: Which of the following is recognized as one of the core freedoms guaranteed under the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR)?
options: Freedom of peaceful assembly and association
Freedom to bear unlicensed concealed weapons
Freedom to disregard valid judicial rulings
questions.explain: **Freedom of peaceful assembly and association** (Article 20 of the UDHR) guarantees the right of citizens to meet peacefully and form or join associations, trade unions, and political organizations.

questions.q: A citizen arrested and detained by security personnel for several months without being charged to a court of law has suffered a violation of the freedom from...
questions.explain: Article 9 of the UDHR and Section 35 of the Nigerian Constitution protect individuals against **arbitrary arrest and detention**. Holding a suspect indefinitely without charging them before a competent court violates this core freedom.

questions.q: The global importance of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) lies primarily in the fact that it...
options: serves as the universal benchmark and foundation for human rights standards worldwide.
dissolves all sovereign national borders between member countries.
places all national armed forces under the direct command of the UN.
prohibits member nations from having independent constitutions.
questions.explain: The **UDHR** acts as a common standard of achievement for all peoples and nations, establishing a baseline of basic rights that national constitutions and international treaties are modeled upon.

questions.q: The statutory body established by the Federal Government of Nigeria to investigate human rights violations and enforce rights protection is the...
questions.explain: The **National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)** was established by the NHRC Act of 1995 to promote, monitor, and protect human rights, investigate abuses, and assist victims in Nigeria.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct

questions.q: Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) and civil society groups support the principles of the UDHR primarily by...
options: sentencing human rights violators to prison terms.
monitoring abuses, educating citizens, and providing legal aid to victims.
commanding military personnel during civil disturbances.
questions.explain: Human rights NGOs (such as Amnesty International and SERAP) promote the UDHR through **civic enlightenment, public advocacy, monitoring and reporting abuses**, and offering legal aid to victims whose rights have been infringed.

questions.q: During an outbreak of a deadly and highly contagious epidemic, the government may lawfully restrict citizens' freedom of movement in order to...
options: raise emergency revenue via movement fines.
safeguard public health and general welfare.
prevent citizens from buying foreign commodities.
questions.explain: Human rights are not absolute. Quarantines and curfews during infectious disease outbreaks are constitutional limitations permitted strictly to protect **public health and general welfare**.

questions.q: Under which of the following circumstances is the state constitutionally permitted to suspend or curtail certain fundamental human rights?
options: When an opposition party challenges an executive appointment
During a legitimately proclaimed state of emergency or wartime
When a citizen chooses to convert to another religious faith
During regular annual budget deliberations in parliament
questions.explain: Section 45 of the Nigerian Constitution provides that rights (such as privacy, expression, assembly, and movement) may be derogated from during periods of **national emergency, war, or public disasters** to maintain state security.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct

questions.q: Which of the following is **NOT** a legitimate constitutional limitation on the exercise of human rights?
options: A lawful sentence of imprisonment passed by a competent court of law
Measures taken to maintain public safety during civil unrest
A citizen's refusal to vote for candidates of the ruling political party
Laws enacted to protect the reputation and freedoms of other citizens
questions.explain: Political preference and voting choice are democratic freedoms. A citizen cannot have their fundamental human rights legally curtailed simply for refusing to support or vote for the ruling party.
